newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to convert debt to euros in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Germany to convert debt to euros in 1999.

text.p: Germany is to convert its stock of debt from marks into euros from the start of 1999, the launch deadline for Europe's monetary union, a finance ministry spokesman said on Monday.

The Handelsblatt newspaper reported the ministry had dropped its objections to an early conversion largely due to the example of France and the Netherlands, which have already announced plans to convert their debt to euros.
"The Handelsblatt story is basically true, but the details have to be worked out," the ministry spokesman said.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel is understood to have discussed the debt conversion project at a meeting in Bonn with leading bankers last Wednesday.

An official in the economics department of the Association of German Banks, said, "We can't confirm it but the government has been under pressure from the Bundesbank which has warned it would be a dangerous move not to do so."

Refraining from converting the debt to euros poses the danger that whole segments of the bond market could move to France or Britain because trading volumes in old German debt would dry up as no new paper would be issued in marks.
"They are working on it and everything looks as if the decision will go in that direction although the official announcement will have to be made by the government," the association official said.
